canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop an in-house chromogenic anti-factor Xa assay for UFH monitoring.
The study aimed to establish a laboratory-specific APTT therapeutic range calibrated to anti-factor Xa 0.3–0.7 IU/mL.
The study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory predictors of APTT–anti-factor Xa classification discordance using random forest and logistic regression.
From March through September 2024, the investigators prospectively collected 190 blood samples from 110 consecutively enrolled hospitalized patients receiving continuous intravenous UFH.

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults aged at least 18 years.
Eligible participants had received intravenous UFH for at least 24 hours.
Eligible participants had both APTT and anti-factor Xa testing performed within 4 hours of blood collection.

population.label: Reported sample allocation across derivation and modeling datasets

canonical_statement: Platelet-poor plasma was prepared by centrifugation at 2,000 × g for 15 minutes at 15–20 °C, aliquoted, and stored at −80 °C.
Normal pooled plasma was prepared from 280 healthy volunteers with normal coagulation parameters and stored at −80 °C.

The in-house assay used a two-stage chromogenic method in which heparin–antithrombin neutralized added bovine factor Xa and residual factor Xa cleaved S-2732; absorbance at 405 nm was inversely related to heparin concentration.
Assay optimization varied factor Xa, S-2732, buffer composition, pH, BSA, PEG-6000, sample-to-reagent ratios, and reaction times to optimize sensitivity and linear range.
Precision was assessed at 0.30, 0.70, and 1.35 IU/mL with 20 within-run measurements and duplicate testing twice daily for 20 days; acceptance criteria were within-run CV <5% and between-run CV <10%.
Analytical sensitivity testing used CLSI EP17-A2 procedures for LoB, LoD, and LoQ; LoQ candidates were required to meet relative MAD ≤30%, probability of detection ≥95%, and total error ≤40%.
Linearity was evaluated from the LoQ to 1.35 IU/mL using serial mixtures and duplicate measurements, with measured values regressed against expected values.

Method comparison tested 80 anonymized plasma specimens with both the in-house and STA-Liquid Anti-Xa systems using correlation, Bland–Altman agreement, paired testing, and regression, following CLSI EP09c.

population.label: Routine diagnostic plasma specimens used for method comparison

canonical_statement: The 190 specimens were randomly allocated in SPSS to an 80-sample APTT-range derivation set and a 110-sample concordance/predictive-modeling set.
APTT therapeutic-range derivation used linear regression of APTT on anti-factor Xa and ROC analyses at anti-factor Xa thresholds of 0.3 and 0.7 IU/mL.

population.label: APTT therapeutic-range derivation specimens from UFH-treated patients

canonical_statement: APTT–anti-factor Xa concordance was defined as agreement in subtherapeutic, therapeutic, or supratherapeutic classification; overall agreement and Cohen κ were planned.

outcome.definition: Agreement across subtherapeutic, therapeutic, and supratherapeutic categories

canonical_statement: Predictive modeling used 10 candidate variables: age, sex, BMI, fibrinogen, antithrombin III, D-dimer, CRP, eGFR, triglycerides, and total cholesterol.
The random forest model used bootstrap sampling, class balancing, permutation importance, out-of-bag validation, and five-fold cross-validation.

Multivariable logistic regression entered all 10 predictors, used backward elimination while retaining antithrombin III and fibrinogen, assessed VIF, Cook distance, Hosmer–Lemeshow fit, and used five-fold cross-validation.

The authors explicitly characterized the predictive modeling as exploratory and hypothesis-generating because 64 discordant events across 10 predictors yielded approximately 6.4 events per variable, below the cited minimum of 10.
The optimized reagent system used bovine factor Xa at 0.9 IU/mL and chromogenic substrate S-2732 at 0.43 mmol/L.
The optimized sample-to-reagent volumes were 5 µL sample, 40 µL reagent 1, and 100 µL reagent 2.
The optimized incubation time was 90 seconds.
The chromogenic detection reaction stabilized after approximately 55 seconds.
The in-house calibration curve had R² 0.99883 with equation Y = −0.01181 + 1.00678X.
The STA-Liquid Anti-Xa calibration curve had R² 0.99854; the main text reports equation Y = −0.00387 + 1.00596X.
Intra-assay precision at QC 1.35 IU/mL had a coefficient of variation of 1.15%.
Intra-assay precision at QC 0.70 IU/mL had a coefficient of variation of 2.52%.
Intra-assay precision at QC 0.30 IU/mL had a coefficient of variation of 4.32%.
Inter-assay precision at QC 1.35 IU/mL had a coefficient of variation of 1.25%.
Inter-assay precision at QC 0.70 IU/mL had a coefficient of variation of 2.06%.
Inter-assay precision at QC 0.30 IU/mL had a coefficient of variation of 4.03%.
The limit of blank was 0.073 IU/mL based on 60 blank measurements.
The limit of detection was 0.080 IU/mL based on 60 low-concentration measurements.
The limit of quantitation was established at 0.10 IU/mL; this was the lowest tested concentration meeting all three MAD, POD, and total-error criteria.

Among patients with APTT >90 seconds, 38% were reported to be within the therapeutic anti-factor Xa range.
Among 110 paired measurements, 46 (41.8%) were concordant and 64 (58.2%) were discordant between APTT and anti-factor Xa therapeutic classifications.
The concordant classifications included 8 subtherapeutic, 32 therapeutic, and 6 supratherapeutic pairs.
Acute coronary syndrome patients had an APTT–anti-factor Xa classification discordance rate of 52.6%.
VTE treatment/prophylaxis patients had an APTT–anti-factor Xa classification discordance rate of 54.2%.

Hemodialysis/CRRT patients had an APTT–anti-factor Xa classification discordance rate of 75.0%.
Other indications patients had an APTT–anti-factor Xa classification discordance rate of 56.0%.
The difference in discordance rates between ICU/surgical indications (73.3%–75.0%) and medical indications (52.6%–54.2%) was not statistically significant (p = 0.156).

canonical_statement: The discussion reports Cohen κ = 0.242 for APTT–anti-factor Xa classification agreement.
The authors report that the in-house monitoring system completes analysis within 5 minutes.
A preliminary cost analysis reported reagent costs of approximately US$2.00 per test, including calibrators, quality controls, and consumables.
The authors conclude that the in-house anti-factor Xa assay had analytical performance comparable to commercial systems.
The authors conclude that poor categorical agreement between APTT and anti-factor Xa highlights limitations of APTT for UFH monitoring.
The authors state that the predictive models are hypothesis-generating and should not guide clinical practice without rigorous prospective validation.
The study was single-center with a limited sample size of 110 patients and 64 discordant events, creating risk of overfitting and institution-specific results.
The cross-sectional design could not assess dynamic changes over time.
The study did not collect bleeding or thrombotic event outcomes, preventing verification that monitoring discordance predicts patient outcomes.
The predictive models had only internal cross-validation and no external validation.
The study was funded by ZONCI Technology Development Co., Ltd., Beijing, China.

One author (HR) was employed by Beijing ZONCI Technology Development Co., Ltd.; the sponsor was involved in study design but was reported to have no role in data collection, analysis, interpretation, or manuscript writing.
The authors state that the original contributions are included in the article or supplementary material and that further inquiries may be directed to the corresponding author.
The article states that generative AI was not used in the creation of the manuscript.
